home.title: CARTAN — Spacecraft serviceability research
home.description: CARTAN investigates interrupted spacecraft module exchange, uncertain retention and electrical isolation. Explore the research question, concepts and evidence boundaries.

question.title: The research question — CARTAN
question.description: What is safe to do when a spacecraft module exchange is interrupted? CARTAN separates physical state, observation, command and inferred belief.

laboratory.title: Module exchange concepts — CARTAN Laboratory
laboratory.description: Explore the proposed module, retention, electrical isolation and transfer support in CARTAN’s component study. Concept geometry is not validated hardware.

interruption.title: Interrupted exchange and uncertain state — CARTAN
interruption.description: Inspect physical state, observations, commands and belief in an explicitly synthetic CARTAN fixture. The example is not a measured experiment or hardware result.

evidence.title: Evidence and explicit unknowns — CARTAN
evidence.description: Understand what CARTAN’s public interface does and does not establish. Missing records, planned work and inconclusive examples remain distinct from evidence.

comparison.title: Baseline comparison protocol — CARTAN
comparison.description: CARTAN’s proposed comparison considers conventional control, additional sensing and passive interlocks. No comparative performance result is claimed.

sources.title: Primary research sources — CARTAN
sources.description: Follow the primary sources informing CARTAN’s spacecraft serviceability research, with explicit distinctions between published methods and CARTAN’s own evidence.

vision.title: Spacecraft that can change — CARTAN vision
vision.description: CARTAN’s long-term ambition is spacecraft maintenance, upgrades and reconfiguration. The imagery is conceptual; no flight architecture or capability is established.
